newsitem.title: POLAND: IB Austria rates Polfa Kutno "reduce".
newsitem.headline: IB Austria rates Polfa Kutno "reduce".

text.p: Investmentbank Austria has given Polish drug maker Polfa Kutno a "reduce" rating, saying the stock was due for a correction after a recent price rise.
"After the sharp increase in the share price, Polfa is now overvalued compared both to its domestic rival Jelfa as well as its regional peers," the report dated March 20 said.
In its previous report IB Austria had given Polfa Kutno a buy rating.
IB Austria said Polfa Kutno would lift net profit to 20.9 million zlotys this year and 28.4 million zlotys next year from 16.2 million zlotys in 1996.
It said sales would rise to 222.5 million zlotys this year and 300.4 million next year from 171.2 million in 1996.
IB Austria said earnings per share would rise to 7.5 and 10.2 zlotys from 6.4 in 1996 with Polfa's price-earnings ratio falling to 15.1 and 11.1 in the two years from 17.7 in 1996.

It said Polfa should be helped by the long-awaited price liberalisation expected next year and the upgrading of its manufacturing facilities which should help it lift exports to 10 percent from the current three percent by the year 2000.
